title: From gut microbiome to aging brain: Butyrate as a neurogeroscience effector
title_zh: 从肠道微生物组到衰老大脑：丁酸盐作为神经衰老学效应因子
abstract: Aging-related cognitive decline is increasingly linked to disruption of the microbiome-gut-brain axis, in which age-associated dysbiosis progressively reduces butyrate production, a short-chain fatty acid and central neuroactive metabolite generated by bacterial fermentation of dietary fiber. Experimental studies indicate that butyrate can influence multiple processes relevant to brain aging, including histone deacetylase activity, neuroinflammatory signaling, microglial phenotypes, blood-brain barrier integrity, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis. Through these mechanisms, butyrate may modulate several molecular and cellular processes involved in brain aging, although evidence for direct causal effects in the human brain remains limited. Preclinical studies report neuroprotective effects across several models of aging and neurological disease; however, direct evidence in humans remains limited and largely associative or indirect. Therefore, this review critically synthesizes current evidence on microbiome-derived butyrate in brain aging, encompassing its microbial production and age-related alterations, molecular and cellular mechanisms, associations with neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric conditions, and emerging strategies for therapeutic modulation and delivery. It examines emerging biotechnological strategies - including prodrug design, nanoparticle- and liposomal-based delivery systems, gut-targeted formulations, and microbiome engineering - all developed to overcome the blood-brain barrier and restore therapeutically relevant butyrate concentrations in the aging brain. By bridging fundamental microbiome biology and translational neuroscience, this review positions butyrate as a mechanistically grounded neurogeroscience effector and charts a roadmap for its application in promoting brain health across the aging continuum.
abstract_zh: 与年龄相关的认知衰退越来越与微生物组-肠道-大脑轴的失调相关，其中与年龄相关的失衡逐步降低丁酸盐的产生，丁酸盐是一种短链脂肪酸，也是由细菌对膳食纤维发酵产生的中心神经活性代谢物。实验研究表明，丁酸盐可以影响与大脑衰老相关的多种过程，包括组蛋白去乙酰化酶活性、神经炎症信号、小胶质细胞表型、血脑屏障完整性、突触可塑性和神经发生。通过这些机制，丁酸盐可能调节涉及大脑衰老的多种分子和细胞过程，尽管在人脑中直接因果效应的证据仍有限。临床前研究报告了在多种衰老和神经疾病模型中的神经保护作用；然而，在人类中的直接证据仍有限，主要是关联性或间接性。因此，本综述批判性地综合了微生物来源的丁酸盐在大脑衰老中的现有证据，涵盖其微生物产生和年龄相关变化、分子和细胞机制、与神经退行性和神经精神疾病的关联，以及用于治疗调节和递送的创新策略。它考察了新兴的生物技术策略——包括前药设计、纳米粒子和脂质体递送系统、肠道靶向配方以及微生物组工程——所有这些都旨在克服血脑屏障并在衰老大脑中恢复具有治疗意义的丁酸盐浓度。通过将基础微生物组生物学与转化神经科学相结合，本综述将丁酸盐定位为具有机制基础的神经衰老学效应因子，并勾画了其在促进整个衰老过程中的大脑健康应用路线图。
